sections.h2: Where does a Williams County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
The Williams County Recorder's Office is on the second floor of the courthouse at One Courthouse Square in Bryan, OH 43506, and the phone is 419-636-3259. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the last documents are accepted for recording at 4:00 p.m.

The office makes a permanent record of every document that conveys or encumbers land in the county, and it indexes each one so that a title search can follow the chain of ownership. Williams County is the Ohio corner that touches Michigan and Indiana. Hillsdale County, Michigan lies to the north, DeKalb and Steuben counties in Indiana to the west, and Fulton, Henry and Defiance counties in Ohio to the east and south. The county seat and largest city is Bryan.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Williams County?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2025 the Recorder's page lists $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page. The $5.00 increase is the preservation surcharge that Senate Bill 94 allowed under R.C. 317.32. The page adds that $4.00 reference fees and the standardization guidelines still apply.

Charges listed on the Williams County Recorder's pages
ItemAmount
Recording, first two pages$39.00
Each additional page$8.00

Document that fails page format rules$20.00 extra
Copy made in person$0.25 per page

Certified copies cost what the Ohio Revised Code sets and are listed on the Recorder's fees page.

sections.h2: Which page format rules can add $20 to a Williams County recording?
sections.html:
Ohio law in R.C. 317.114 sets a standard layout so recording information has a place on every instrument. A document that misses it is still recorded, with an extra $20 collected. The Williams County Recorder lists these guidelines:

  • Black or blue ink only, with no highlighting.
  • Computer type of at least 10 point.
  • One inch margins on each side and the bottom.
  • A 3 inch top margin on the first page and 1.5 inches on additional pages.
  • Paper no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches and no smaller than 8.5 by 11.

The rules do not apply to documents signed before the law took effect on July 1, 2009, court or taxing authority papers, state or federal documents, DD214 discharge papers or plats. A seller whose attorney or title company drafts the deed rarely has to worry, but a homemade deed often does.

sections.h2: What must happen before the Williams County Recorder accepts a deed?
sections.html:
The Recorder will accept a conveyance by mail only if the Engineer's and Auditor's stamps are already on it. That covers deeds, land contracts, easements and affidavits. The Auditor provides the conveyance information after the Engineer's Office approves the legal description, and for many documents the Treasurer must first confirm that taxes on the parcel have been paid.

  • County Engineer: reviews the legal description on certain documents.
  • Auditor, One Courthouse Square, 419-636-5639: sets the conveyance charge once the description is approved. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Treasurer: validates that taxes have been paid.
  • Recorder: records and indexes the stamped deed.

Under R.C. 319.202 the grantee files a statement of value, and the grantor pays the conveyance fee. The Auditor's page prints a conveyance fee of $4 per $1,000 of the purchase price and a transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel or deed. New conveyance standards took effect January 1, 2026, and the Auditor's page links to them.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Williams County housing?
sections.html:
Williams County had 36,549 residents estimated for July 2025, down 1.5 percent from the April 2020 base. QuickFacts counts 15,476 households and 16,659 housing units, and 76.3 percent of homes are owner occupied.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $150,000.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,163, and $462 without.
  • Median gross rent: $791.
  • Median household income: $61,048 in 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.8 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 44.

Density is 88.2 people per square mile across about 421 square miles of land, a rural pattern, with places such as Nettle Lake and Lake Seneca, both census designated places. Alvordton, Kunkle and Pulaski are the others.

sections.h2: How can a Williams County owner get a copy of a deed?
sections.html:
Anyone can walk into the Recorder's Office and copy a public document, a deed included, for $0.25 per page. Staff will help find the record. A written request costs $2.00 per page and must give the volume and page, which you can find on the Ohio Land Records index. Include a check or money order and a self addressed stamped envelope, because the office cannot fill copy requests by phone or email.

The online index covers recorded documents from October 25, 1999 forward, and new entries should show within 24 hours of recording. It shows the owner, document type and property description, not the image itself. A certified copy is available, though a plain copy costs the same $0.25 per page in person.

The Recorder warns about a company in Sioux Falls, South Dakota that mailed a "Deed Processing Notice" asking homeowners for $83 for a copy of their deed. Deeds are public, and anyone can pick up a copy for you at the courthouse.

sections.h2: How do Williams County taxes and the Recorder fit into a cash sale?
sections.html: Every sale in the county, whatever the funding, passes through the same chain of stamps. Ask the Treasurer for a paid tax confirmation, bring the legal description to the Engineer, carry the deed to the Auditor, then file with the Recorder before 4:00 p.m. Because the Recorder cannot give legal advice and the office is barred from preparing documents, a closing attorney or title company should draft the deed.

sections.h2: How is a Williams County recording fee divided under state law?
sections.html:
The statute behind the $39.00 figure is R.C. 317.32. It sets a base fee of $17 and a housing trust fund fee of $17 for the first two pages, and $4 plus $4 for each later page, which adds up to $34 and $8. A county may then add a document preservation surcharge of up to $5, and Williams County does, bringing the first two pages to $39.00. The surcharge is meant to pay for preserving and digitizing records and for online access to them.

Other items in the same section matter at a closing. A marginal reference carries a base fee of $2 and a housing trust fund fee of $2, which matches the $4.00 reference fee the Recorder mentions. Certifying a copy costs $1 plus $1 per page, and the seal adds $0.50 plus $0.50.

sections.h2: How old is Williams County, and who runs it?
sections.html:
The county was created on April 1, 1820 and organized on February 2, 1824, and it is named for David Williams, one of the men who captured John Andre in the Revolutionary War. Three county commissioners oversee the departments, and Bryan holds the courthouse. By total area it is the 53rd largest of Ohio's counties, and the Williams County Airport sits about two nautical miles east of downtown Bryan.

The land records matter because the county is old enough that a deed from the nineteenth century may sit in the chain of title. The Recorder keeps documentation back to the beginning of Williams County land ownership, even though the online index starts in 1999.

faqs.q: What are the Williams County Recorder's hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The last documents are accepted for recording at 4:00 p.m. The office is on the second floor of the courthouse at One Courthouse Square in Bryan.

faqs.q: How much does Williams County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page since January 1, 2025, plus a $4.00 reference fee where one applies. A deed that breaks the page format rules adds $20.

faqs.q: What is the Williams County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor lists $4 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel or deed. It is paid at the Auditor's office after the Engineer approves the legal description.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Williams County Recorder?
faqs.a: Only if the Engineer's and Auditor's stamps are already on it. Without those stamps the Recorder will not accept a conveyance by mail.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my Williams County deed?
faqs.a: Visit the Recorder in person and pay $0.25 per page, or mail a written request with the volume and page, a check or money order, and a stamped return envelope at $2.00 per page.
